info.name: Labor Project Backend
info.description:
Postman collection for Labor Project Backend. baseUrl defaults to http://localhost:8080 for local development — change the baseUrl/wsBaseUrl variables to the shared droplet's domain (see README > Deploying to DigitalOcean) to test against the shared dev/test deployment instead.
Every request shows its contract explicitly in that request: method, URL, required headers, query params, and body.
Protected requests use Header: Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}.
Run Auth > POST /api/auth/login first to get AccessToken and RefreshToken.
Every request also accepts optional X-Request-Id and X-Client-Version headers for log correlation/debugging (added automatically below). X-Client-Type is required only on the /api/auth endpoints that run before an access token exists (login, login/confirm-force, refresh) — see each request's Headers line.

Token lifecycle (added 2026-09-16): Each session has an absolute cap counted from its first login and never extended by /api/auth/refresh no matter how often it succeeds — Worker: 7 days, Admin: 24 hours. Every protected response also adds header X-Should-Refresh: true once the AccessToken in use is close to expiring (default threshold: 2 minutes) — call POST /api/auth/refresh right away when you see it. Worker WebSocket connections (GET /ws/workers) get the same signal as a TOKEN_NEARING_EXPIRY event for the case where the app is only listening on the socket and issuing no REST calls at all.

Method: POST

Auth: No auth required
Headers: Content-Type: application/json, X-Client-Type (required, worker_app), X-Request-Id (optional, correlation id), X-Client-Version (optional)
Query: None
Body: JSON: LoginChallengeToken, DeviceId, DeviceName, optional FcmToken, optional Platform
Notes: Use only after login returns ACTIVE_SESSION_EXISTS with a LoginChallengeToken. If FcmToken is sent, backend revokes the old session push token and stores the new token for this WorkerCode. If Mobile does not have an FCM token yet, omit it here and call POST /api/auth/push-token after Firebase SDK returns the token. The push notification sent to the old device (telling it it was signed out) is best-effort only: if it fails for any reason (Firebase/network issues, invalid credential, expired token, etc.), this request still returns 200 and still revokes the old session and creates the new one.

Headers: Content-Type: application/json, X-Client-Type (required, {{clientType}}), X-Request-Id (optional, correlation id), X-Client-Version (optional)
Query: None
Body: JSON: RefreshToken
Notes: Returns a new AccessToken and RefreshToken (RefreshToken rotates every call; the old one can no longer be used). This never extends the session's absolute cap (Worker 7d / Admin 24h from first login); once that's reached this call returns 401 and the client must log in again.

request.description:
Method: POST
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/admin/users
Auth: Required via Authorization header
Headers: Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}. Do not set Content-Type manually for multipart/form-data; Postman sets the boundary., X-Request-Id (optional, correlation id), X-Client-Version (optional)
Query: None
Body: multipart/form-data. ImageUrl (text, optional) — leave blank or omit entirely for null; the frontend passes a URL string here (e.g. a pre-uploaded CDN link), not a file. Text fields: FullName, Phone, Nationality, ShirtType, ShirtNumber, TimeWork, optional WorkStartDate, Status.
Response: message only, Worker created successfully.
Notes: Admin only. username defaults to WorkerCode generated from nationality + ShirtType + ShirtNumber, such as MN000012. nationality accepts Myanmar or Cambodia. ShirtType accepts Navy, Blue, or Green. ShirtNumber is unique and cannot be reused. Worker password is always the hashed value of phone, and phone is saved to accounts.phone. TimeWork Morning uses preset 08:00-18:00 and TimeWork Evening uses preset 18:00-08:00. WorkStartDate is optional; if omitted, backend uses the current Bangkok date. ImageUrl is saved as-is to accounts.image_url — no upload/processing happens server-side for this field. A real binary file upload is still accepted too, via a separate multipart file field named Image (not shown in this example) which the backend saves under /uploads/workers and uses instead of ImageUrl if both are sent.

Auth: Admin access token with jobs:wait permission
Body: Dispatch (required boolean), ReasonCode (required, non-empty), ReasonText (optional — may be omitted or sent as null)
Notes: Toggles the vehicle job's dispatch. Dispatch=false puts it back to "waiting to unload" (DispatchNow=false, Status=WAIT): cancels every currently active TicketJobAssignment for the team and puts the whole team back at the front of the FIFO queue, then runs a dispatch pass so those freed workers can pick up other already-dispatched vehicle jobs immediately. Dispatch=true puts it back to dispatched (DispatchNow=true, Status=WORKING) and calls workers from the queue for this vehicle job right away — same mechanics as Gate creating a job with Dispatch=true; the team pulled in may be a different one, depending on who is at the front of the queue at that moment. Either direction is only allowed while the whole required team has NOT YET finished checking in (still PENDING/ACCEPTED/partially SCANNED — "wait_team"); once every required worker has scanned in, dispatch can no longer be changed (409 VEHICLE_JOB_ALREADY_STARTED), since no booth could still be un-started past that point. Returns 409 VEHICLE_JOB_CLOSED if the vehicle job is already COMPLETED/CANCELLED. Recorded in AdminActionLog (Metadata.Dispatch records the direction) and appears in GET /api/admin/vehicle-jobs/history Timeline as an ADMIN_ACTION event.
Response: Message, TicketNumber, Status, DispatchNow, WorkerToQueue[] (workers still within their shift, sent back to the queue) and WorkerToOpenapp[] (workers whose shift had already ended, sent to open_app) — both only populated when Dispatch=false, ReasonCode, ReasonText.

request.description:
Method: POST
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/admin/vehicle-jobs/{{ticketNumber}}/release-workers
Auth: Admin access token with jobs:release_workers permission
Body: ReasonCode (required), ReasonText (optional)
Notes: Releases the dispatched worker team back to the FIFO queue once every booth has been submitted — status DELIVERED (submitted, awaiting vendor confirmation), COMPLETED (vendor confirmed), or CANCELLED. Does NOT require vendor confirmation first: the worker's physical duty ends the moment they submit counted quantities, so the team can be released while a booth is still DELIVERED and waiting on the vendor — if the vendor later rejects, the Worker (or Admin via override-count) can still resubmit regardless of whether the original team was released. Also does not wait for the whole vehicle job to close, Gate to signal no more Business Tickets, or per-Business-Ticket financial finalize — money is settled later independently. Booth/ticket status is unaffected (stays DELIVERED/WORKING in Work History until the vendor actually confirms or times out), but the VehicleJob's own status moves from WORKING to RELEASED (non-terminal) so it is excluded from FIFO dispatch until Gate submits a new booth for this ticketNumber (reopens dispatch automatically, same as from WAIT) or Admin reopens dispatch via /wait — this prevents the just-released team, or any other queued worker, from being immediately redispatched back onto the same vehicle job. Workers are appended to the BACK of the FIFO queue ordered by AcceptedAt (earliest accept first), the same relative ordering used when they first joined the queue — not by the order their TicketJobAssignment rows were created/dispatched. Returns 409 if the vehicle job is already closed (VEHICLE_JOB_CLOSED), has no booths yet (NO_SUBMITTED_BOOTHS), has a booth still WAIT/WORKING/REJECT — REJECT means an unresolved vendor rejection the worker must fix and resubmit first (BOOTHS_NOT_SUBMITTED), or has no releasable workers (NO_RELEASABLE_WORKERS). Recorded in AdminActionLog and appears in GET /api/admin/vehicle-jobs/history Timeline as an ADMIN_ACTION event plus a WORKER_RELEASED event per worker.
Response: Message, TicketNumber, ReleasedWorkerCodes[] (ordered by AcceptedAt), ReasonCode, ReasonText.

Two independent FCM notifications are involved, each with its own timing field and its own "already sent" tracker: the ReleaseMessage notice fires at ReleaseNotificationAt (omit/null = send synchronously in this request and set ReleaseNotificationSentAt; a future time schedules it via BullMQ instead, and must not be later than ForceUpdateAt); the force-update notice is a standard-pattern-only FCM that fires automatically at ForceUpdateAt itself, tracked independently via ForceUpdateNotificationSentAt, and only scheduled when ForceUpdateAt is set. Neither notification ever activates the version early. ReleaseAt is metadata only (UI/History display), not a trigger for anything. request.description:
Method: POST
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/gate/tickets
Auth: Gate Basic Auth using {{gateClientId}} / {{gateClientSecret}}. Create credentials with Admin Settings > POST /api/admin/gate-clients first.
Headers: Content-Type: application/json, X-Request-Id (optional, correlation id), X-Client-Version (optional)
Body: One request per Business Ticket (TicketNo), always against exactly one MarketCode. TicketNumber and TicketNo must both be exactly 14 digits, numbers only. A vehicle (TicketNumber) may generate multiple Business Tickets over time as it unloads at different markets — send the same TicketNumber again with a new TicketNo; no duplicate vehicle job is created. TicketNo is scoped to one market: sending the same TicketNo again under the same TicketNumber and the same MarketCode (while that Ticket is still active) appends the new Booths/Products into the existing Business Ticket instead of creating a new one. Appending a BoothCode that already exists in that Ticket is rejected with GATE_BOOTH_ALREADY_EXISTS_IN_TICKET, and appending after that Ticket's worker roster is already locked is rejected with GATE_TICKET_ROSTER_LOCKED. Sending the same TicketNo again for a *different* MarketCode is always rejected with GATE_TICKET_ALREADY_EXISTS. If a Ticket was created with wrong data (wrong market, needs a full redo), an Admin must cancel it first (POST /api/admin/vehicle-jobs/assignment/cancel with TicketNumber+TicketNo); once cancelled, that exact TicketNo becomes free again and Gate can resend it under the same TicketNumber (any MarketCode) to create a brand-new Business Ticket — the cancelled Ticket is kept untouched as history. WorkerCount for a Ticket is the MAX (not sum) across every product in every booth of that Ticket, recomputed as the MAX between the Ticket's current value and this request's own MAX. Required root fields: TicketNumber, TicketNo, TicketCreatedAt, BoothCount, MarketCode, LicensePlate, LicensePlateProvince, VehicleTypeCode, VehicleTypeName, Booths, Dispatch. Gate does not send a ticket count — the number of active Business Tickets under a TicketNumber is simply however many active markets have a Ticket. Each Booth requires BoothCode and Products. Each Product requires ProductCode, PackageCode, Quantity. BoothCount must equal Booths.length. BoothCode cannot be duplicated in the same request. ProductCode + PackageCode cannot be duplicated inside the same booth.
Financial boundary: Gate Quantity is operational/dispatch quantity only. The backend may snapshot the applicable Master rate internally at Gate Create, but Gate Create does not calculate or expose StallPayment, WorkerPayment, OrderRemainder, Fund, or final financial amounts. Financialization happens only after worker-confirmed quantities are vendor-confirmed or auto-confirmed.
Response: Result, TicketNumber, Ticket, Market, Booths with operational product data, WorkerCount for dispatch, and Qr (DriverQrToken only, shared across the whole vehicle). Workers check in by scanning the barcode already printed on the physical Gate paper ticket (Ticket.TicketNo) — no separate QR field is generated. Ticket.Status is derived from Dispatch only: true = unload_now, false = waiting_unload.
Idempotency: Gate transaction ref is derived from the full request payload (not just TicketNumber+TicketNo), because the same TicketNumber+TicketNo+MarketCode can legitimately be sent again with different content to append. Same payload returns REPLAYED. Same TicketNumber+TicketNo+MarketCode with different content is appended rather than rejected.
Vehicle closing: since Gate never signals "more Tickets coming," intake for a vehicle closes automatically as soon as its first Business Ticket is created. Once every known Business Ticket's booths are terminal, the vehicle job completes and its workers return to queue automatically. There is no separate close endpoint.
Notes: Saves gateResult, ticketNumber, ticketNo, marketCode, first BoothCode, first ProductCode, first PackageCode, workerCount, and driverQrToken into collection variables.

Also readable from Markets[].TicketNo in the accept response or CurrentJob.Markets[].TicketNo from GET /api/workers/me/status. It is a real business identifier (not a generated secret), resolved safely by scoping the lookup to this worker's own current vehicle assignment. Scanning any one Business Ticket under the vehicle checks in the whole team.
Response: Status, WorkerStatus, WorkerCode, TicketNumber, TicketNo, TeamScan. TicketNo echoes back the exact Business Ticket this request scanned (never any other TicketNo under the same TicketNumber, even when the vehicle has several). Normally { "Status": "SCANNED", "WorkerStatus": "waiting_team", "WorkerCode": "MN000142", "TicketNumber": "20260804000001", "TicketNo": "20260804000002", "TeamScan": { "WorkersRequired": 3, "CheckedInCount": 1, "RemainingCount": 2, "IsReady": false } }.
Notes: Checks worker into the job only while ScanDeadlineAt is still valid. Default scan window comes from WorkerScanDeadlineMinutes after accept. After this worker scans, WorkerStatus is waiting_team until every active/eligible assignment in the team has scanned, then working. Admin SSE and the assigned Worker (via WebSocket/FCM push) both receive ASSIGNMENT_SCAN_DEADLINE_WARNING when an ACCEPTED worker has not checked in and remaining scan time is below WorkerScanWarningBeforeMinutes. In a multi-worker team, once the first worker checks in, remaining ACCEPTED workers receive ASSIGNMENT_SCAN_DEADLINE_SHORTENED and their ScanDeadlineAt/ScanDeadlineUnixMs is shortened by WorkerScanTeamRemainingMinutes from that first check-in. If scan time expires by API call or background timeout, the assignment becomes TIMEOUT and worker status returns to open_app. Admin can extend ScanDeadlineAt/ScanDeadlineUnixMs and the worker can retry with the same TicketNo if the assignment is still ACCEPTED. If active/eligible team scan is ready, vehicle job moves to WORKING. The scan is also recorded on the SCANNED WorkerAssignmentEvent with which TicketNo/MarketCode/MarketName was scanned, auditable later.

request.description:
Method: POST
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/workers/me/assignments/tickets/complete
Auth: Worker access token
Body: TicketNo, BoothCode and Items required. TicketNo names which Business Ticket this submission belongs to — required because two Business Tickets under the same vehicle, against different markets, can legitimately share the same BoothCode; TicketNo plus BoothCode together resolve the exact booth unambiguously. Send BoothCode in body so codes containing / such as OM3/40 do not need URL encoding. Send every ProductCode + PackageCode in the ticket with ConfirmedQuantity counted by the worker.
Package switch: to change a product's package (not just quantity), first call GET /api/workers/me/products/{ProductCode}/packages to find a valid new PackageCode, then send that item with PackageCode set to the new value and OriginalPackageCode set to the PackageCode Gate originally declared for that product line. Backend re-derives the rate snapshot (weight/rate can differ by package) before accepting — an invalid/inactive PackageCode is rejected with 409 PRODUCT_PACKAGE_NOT_FOUND. Items not switching a package only need PackageCode as before.
Financial boundary: This request only records confirmed actual quantities and starts vendor confirmation. It must not create final financial records before vendor confirm or timeout auto-confirm.
Notes: No TicketNumber in the URL — the vehicle is always resolved from this worker's own current active assignment, never from the client. TicketNo and BoothCode come from the accepted/check-in job payload (Markets[].TicketNo / Markets[].Stalls[].BoothCode). Backend resolves each product by ProductCode + PackageCode. The LINE message to the vendor shows both the originally declared package and the new one when a product's package was switched. The response does not expose LINE postback tokens. Vendor confirm completes financialization; vendor reject returns the ticket to REJECT for resubmission.
